Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. projects.description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio — 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.
projects.readmeExcerpt: Claude Code Game Studios Turn a single Claude Code session into a full game development studio. 49 agents. 74 skills. One coordinated AI team. Why This Exists Building a game solo with AI is powerful — but a single chat session has no structure. No one stops you from hardcoding magic numbers, skipping design docs, or writing spaghetti code. There's no QA pass, no design review, no one asking "does this actually fit the game's vision?" Claude Code Game Studios solves this by giving your AI session the structure of a real studio. Instead of one general purpose assistant, you get 49 specialized agents organized into a studio hierarchy — directors who guard the vision, department leads who own their domains, and specialists who do the hands on work. Each agent has defined responsibilities, escalation paths, and quality gates. The result: you still make every decision, but now you have a team

projects.readmeExcerpt: Orkas An open source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving. Orkas is an open source (MIT), local first multi agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the Commander what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent — to work on it together. Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A project holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. To dos split the work between people and agents, Auto advance lets the team take on the next to do by itself, and scheduled automations repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly.
